current_episode.title: BLP:373 They Sold the Company to Their Employees. Now they're Millionaires.

guest.bio_context: Robert joined ESS Companies in 2018 through a relationship formed on a design-build joint venture project with Granite Construction in Colorado. He is a third-generation contractor who earned an engineering degree from Colorado School of Mines, working full-time while attending school his first two years. He brings expertise in earthwork, structures, public delivery, and alternative delivery methods to his co-CEO role.

context.real_quote: Every dollar that's made makes its way to the employee owners, because everybody in between has a stake in the ownership of this company.
key_stats: 168 employees exceeded $500,000 in accounts this year
98 total millionaires in company, 59% work in field
Turnover 10-20% better than industry average (30% or less vs. 50% industry standard)
Revenue grew approximately 340% over last five years
Co-CEO started 8 years ago when company did 1/6th current revenue
$2.8 billion allocated by Missouri for I-70 reconstruction and third lane
I-70 reconstruction completion target: end of 2031
Employees earn approximately 25% of salary annually as ESOP contribution
entities: I-70 corridor (St. Louis to Kansas City)

pending_qa.q: How does employee ownership in construction impact retention compared to industry standards?
pending_qa.r: While exact metrics are difficult to isolate due to seasonal layoffs in the Midwest construction industry, ESS estimates their turnover is about 10 to 20 percent better than other companies. Industry turnover in construction is commonly near 50 percent, especially in craft positions, but ESS operates at 30 percent or less. The ESOP's value becomes clear around year three when employees see their account balances growing significantly, which drives better retention.

pending_qa.q: What revenue growth trajectory has a construction holding company achieved through organic growth and acquisitions?
pending_qa.r: The co-CEO started with the company eight years ago and projects they will do about six times the revenue this year compared to when he started. Additionally, over the last five years the company has grown approximately 340 percent through both organic growth and mergers and acquisitions, now operating about 3,000 employee owners across multiple subsidiaries and brands.

pending_qa.q: What are the largest infrastructure projects currently underway in the Midwest for a heavy civil construction firm?
pending_qa.r: ESS won Project Two of the I-70 reconstruction effort between St. Louis and Kansas City, which is a $608 million design-build job in joint venture with Clarkson Construction, covering about 10 miles of Highway 64 and the 64-70 interchange to Warnton. They recently also won Project 4, stretching through Columbia from the 70-63 interchange to the Rocheport Bridge. The state of Missouri allocated $2.8 billion in general revenue funding to reconstruct all of I-70 and add a third lane, with completion targeted by the end of 2031.

pending_qa.q: Why is the federal gas tax structure inadequate for modern infrastructure funding needs?
pending_qa.r: The gas tax is a flat number of cents per gallon that has never changed since inception, unlike sales tax which scales with price. As inflation occurs, cars become more efficient, and hybrid and electric vehicles proliferate, the funding source for roadway construction decreases year over year. Additionally, Americans pay more for a cell phone than they pay in taxes to drive on the roads used every day, representing a fundamental structural problem that requires a different funding approach to maintain aging infrastructure.

pending_qa.q: What role does trucking and material logistics play in heavy civil construction operations?
pending_qa.r: Trucking is huge for asphalt paving and concrete paving work, requiring enormous quantities of aggregates, oil, cement, and sand moved to job sites. ESS operates about 600 trucks daily including end dumps, side dumps, belly dumps, water wagons, fuel trucks, and low boys. Every construction job is essentially a large logistics job involving material movement. For the I-70 reconstruction alone, thousands of loads of aggregate, oil, cement, and sand need to traverse the road, making material movement a critical component of project execution.

pending_qa.q: Why does a large construction company structure its executive leadership with two co-CEOs?
pending_qa.r: Management teams should be structured to get the job done based on company needs. The two co-CEOs have very complementary backgrounds: one has expertise in heavy asphalt and private negotiated work, while the other brings expertise in earthwork, structures, public delivery, and alternative delivery methods. Given the types of clients served, diverse job constructions, multiple geographic locations, and varied delivery methods, having both skill sets rounded them out very well and proved effective for the company.
